• 23 x USB charging cords of varying lengths (from 6" to 6' long)
• 10 x USB charging bricks (Samsung and Motorola brands.. AKA "the fat boys")
• and a couple of SanDisk microSD cards and adapters

All in all, a great solution, and at a very reasonable price, for organizing your cord chaos.

Bose QuietComfort 20 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones, Samsung and Android Devices, Black The noise cancelling works better than hoped for. However, my ears must be different because none of the different sized ear tips will stay in my ear when I am wearing them to walk or do yard work. I called asking if they have over the ear hooks/adapters to help keep them in place, and there are none.

I normally buy regular over the head earphones, and got these because of their noise cancelling properties and because they looked like they would be more comfortable. Our neighbors have a dog that barks all day long (literally) when they leave their home and I wanted peace and quiet when I go outside now that it is warming up and gardening season is here. Like I said, the noise cancelling works great. But, it only works as long as they stay in my ears, so I am using my husbands Bose OE2 headphones instead.

If my ears would hold the buds, I would LOVE these. They do work as promised. I am just disappointed there is no such thing as an over the ear clip accessory for those of us with ears that don't do well with them.

I called Bose and they are sending me another set of eartips to see if maybe these were just missized or defective.

text_fidelity_a: TOZO T10 Bluetooth 5.3 Wireless Earbuds with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Headphones in Ear Built in Mic Headset Premium Sound with Deep Bass for Sport White (2022 Upgraded) I purchased these several months ago and have found myself reaching for them less and less because of their inconsistent behavior. They'll pair with my phone (Samsung Galaxy S9) just fine with no issue, but the phone has to be in a particular spot for the connection to remain stable. I had it in my inner jacket pocket while snowblowing recently, and if I turned my head too far to the right, the earbuds dropped connection momentarily and skipped my song a bit. If I put them in my snowpants pocket near my waist, it would continually cut out so I couldn't enjoy a full song. I don't have a pacemaker or any other electronic device on my person or near me, and the snowblower is a mechanical gas-powered device without bluetooth, so there's no real reason why the earbuds would be acting oddly under these circumstances. I can't wear them while mowing the lawn on my (gas-powered) riding lawnmower because they cut out all the time. Can't wear them while cleaning in my basement unless I am always in direct line-of-sight to my phone at all times. I haven't even tried using them while exercising but I anticipate another frustrating experience. It's too bad because they fit well, the sound is good, and the charging case is super well-designed and convenient. But I can't rely on them to deliver good sound continuously. I'll probably only use these at my desk (if possible -- haven't even tried that yet) and use my Soundcore bluetooth earbuds for all my other activities. Disappointing experience!
text_fidelity_b: TOZO T10 Bluetooth 5.3 Wireless Earbuds with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Headphones in Ear Built in Mic Headset Premium Sound with Deep Bass for Sport White (2022 Upgraded)

Magellan Triton 400 Waterproof Hiking GPS I have a Garmin e-trex GPS as a backup for my sailboat navigation system so my use of handheld systems has been limited to marine use only. At first I thought this Magellan Trinton 400 system would be a good handheld for marine use. Then I changed my mind.

1. Yes, this 400 is in color... but the battery life is half that of my e-trex and I would much prefer longer battery life than a color screen. This is personal bias of course and may not be of importance to you.

2. I noted the 400 was much larger than my old e-trex and seemed "clunkier".

3. However, the biggest frustration was attemping to link the 400 with my boat's navigation program on my laptop. I simply wasn't able to link and their website help page was close to worthless. Never was able to link. My e-trex links right away.

4. I should have been able to download marine charts to the 400 but after several hours on their website, I was also unable to do this.

5. Finally, it was discouraging to google "Triton 400" and find so many negative comments about the unit and Magellan's support.

For land use, other than the short battery life, it might present a decent option. But for marine use, I'll stick with my Garmin e-trex.
text_fidelity_b: Magellan Triton 400 Waterproof Hiking GPS

Transcend 16 GB Class 6 SDHC Flash Memory Card TS16GSDHC6 I have been using Panasonic SDHC Class 6 4GB cards, and have been pretty happy with them. I decided to get this one just because of the low price and high ratings, and am pleased to find that I agree with the many 5-star reviews.

Some information I didn't see in the other reviews, in case it's of interest: I ran a write test with a big file on my computer, and saw write speeds consistently above 6MB/s, as you ought to expect for a Class 6. (Among other things, that means of course that your camera can get ready for the next shot just that much faster because it's spending less time waiting for the recording to be completed.)

I didn't bother with a read test, since read speed is rarely an issue.

A comment on SD card readers/writers. As many have said, older SD devices, including older cameras, will not work with SDHC cards. My old card adapter (Sandisk 8-in-1) hung when I put this chip in. But my newer adapters (a built-in slot, and an Edge All-in-1) worked just fine. So if you're having trouble, this is possibly the first thing to check.
text_fidelity_b: Transcend 16 GB Class 6 SDHC Flash Memory Card TS16GSDHC6

LotFancy Laptop Cooling Pad with 2 LED Fans Ultra Slim Portable Chill Mat for 13 to 15 Inch Computer, Dual USB Ports I received this as a free review sample and it was sorely needed because the internal fan in my ThinkPad T61 finally died. Note: if you are looking at this as a cure know that many laptops report a fan failure then shut down. In the case of mine, I found that I could press the On/Off button briefly when that happened and it would power back up and boot Windows.

This fan array moves a lot of air, promoting excellent heat transfer. So far it has worked well and I have had no premature shutdowns (although I still have to go through the On/Off button sequence every time I power the ThinkPad up.)

Do be aware that this fan array will interfere with other USB peripherals if you power it directly from your laptop, and especially if you add even more peripherals to the ports integrated into this unit. That is because the power draw form USB ports may exceed the capacity of the laptop, especially if you are running it off an unpowered USB hub. I had that problem when I tried running this, a mouse and a speaker from my laptop. I moved this one to a powered hub and the problem was immediately resolved.

Also, this raises a laptop 1 3/8 inches higher at its lowest setting. For me it took a day to become accustomed to the raised typing height, but since it solved a genuine problem the tradeoff was worth it. Just know that you will need to adjust to that and it may slow down your productivity for a day or two.

If your laptop has a fully functioning internal fan this array will augment that and keep your laptop cool even in unairconditioned spaces on a hot day. That will definitely prolong the life of the internal electronics and the hard drive.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooling Pad with 2 LED Fans Ultra Slim Portable Chill Mat for 13 to 15 Inch Computer, Dual USB Ports

text_fidelity_a:
MarBlue Atlas (new) for Kindle Case, Black (Fits Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle and Kindle Touch) This is a review of both the black and blue MarBlue Atlas Kindle Cases. These are decent cases and have some good things going for them. I wouldn't say they're great cases but they do the job with, what I consider, only a few flaws.

The system for attaching your Kindle to the cover are four very strong and quite tight rubber reinforced elastic cords. I've had several Kindles and numerous cases over the years and as far as four corner case mounts this is the most secure of that style I've ever seen. I had my PaperWhite mounted in this case and shook it violently, over a pillow and ready to catch it should anything happen, and not only did it stay in place it didn't move a fraction of an inch. I was very impressed with that function of the case.

The case exterior is a synthetic leather that truly looks and feels like leather. It is well made, and fairly handsome. Unlike many synthetic products this had no harsh chemical smell. The blue cover looks a little less like leather than the black but it is a very nice shade of blue.

The interior is an attractive, and soft, dark grey microfiber that's quite pleasing to the touch.

The case is held closed or open with a half inch wide cloth elastic that is well attached to the case. This holds the case closed quite well. The hinge area of the case is a bit too large/tall/wide making the case when folded back a little ungainly and if not strapped down it wanted to flop closed.

Inside the case is a nearly three inch wide strap made of the same soft, grey microfiber attached with elastics at both the top and bottom. This comes into use when the case is open you can put your hand or fingers under this strap to read one handed. With my PaperWhite I found this to be slightly uncomfortable making me arch my hand in an odd manner to get my thumb onto the screen. I'm not a fan of the strap, the sections at the top and bottom where it's stitched to the elastic create two lumps that sit directly on the Kindle's screen. They're soft but it's two unnecessary pressure points.

This case does not have the magnet that the Amazon brand case does that turns the kindle on and off when you open it. The power button on my PaperWhite was a little hard to reach with the shape of the case and the location of the mounting strap. It wasn't too difficult to use but it's nowhere near as easy as opening the case and having your Kindle come on.

In conclusion...
The case is decent. It's a little... gappy, the front cover bends when you have your hand in the strap and this creates a gap that will let debris into the case and onto your Kindle. I'm not crazy about the strap but that's more personal preference than anything else. This is a well made decently protective Kindle case.
text_fidelity_b: MarBlue Atlas (new) for Kindle Case, Black (Fits Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle and Kindle Touch)

text_fidelity_a:
ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count This charger works. It comes down to preference in style, and perhaps the going price at the time you are shopping around.

Upon arrival, I immediately unpacked this ACDelco battery charger. It comes with 4 AA batteries, and since I didn't see anything on the package about them being precharged, I went ahead and plugged them into my truck adapter. I was curious how well it would do in my truck (with the included car adapter) and since I knew I was running an errand that would take no more than two hours, I figured it was a good time to try it out.

I plugged them in at 2:10 pm, and saw that the batteries were charging as indicated by the red light. When I got back into my truck (I remembered to look!), the time was 3:05, and the battery indicator light was green, telling me that the batteries were fully charged. So this 55 minute charge time (likely less, since I wasn't in the truck whole time) tells me that it charged faster than anticipated, or the batteries had a little bit of charge on them to begin with, which is more apt the case--which is nice when they can be used right out of the package. Either way, it clearly charges and works fine.

(edit to add..) I see in the lower product description that the batteries come charged. Mine weren't fully charged, but I assume half charge (or more), and my charge time just topped them off. So to test this product further, I grabbed a set of drained rechargeable batteries from another brand that I hadn't gotten around to re-charging yet. I mean, I used them but drained them. I hadn't charged them again yet because I don't care for the charger it came with, so I just keep putting it off. I LIKE THIS CHARGING UNIT, and I will explain after details..

DETAILS!
--This charger charges AA and AAA batteries. It comes with 4 AA batteries and two styles of cords 110-volt wall adapter and 12-volt car adapter

-- The cord measurement for each is as follows:
74" wall charger cord
41" car adapter cord

--Charging Time Per Battery Capacity:
AA 1400mAh - 1800mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AA 1800mAh - 2300mAh: 2-2.5 hours
AAA 600mAh - 750mAh: 1.5 - 2 hours
AAA 750mAh - 1000mAh: 2-2.5 hours

--So, on the face of the charger on the left hand side, there are two indicator lights: one that glows red as the batteries charge, and one that glows green when charged and ready for use. Easy peasy.

--On the right hand side, there is a switch. It is to be set to either 2 batteries, or 4 batteries (+2, +4). Among the rebels among us, I have no idea what happens if we tried charging three batteries! :O

--Within the battery placement area, the slots are numbered. 1 through 4. I wish there were more clarification on this on the product page because I can no longer find the directions it came with. I am thinking that if just two batteries are being used, and they were placed in #1, #2 slots (or #3,#4) AND the indicator switched was in place for 2 batteries, does the charging juice primarily go to those spot (so as to keep with the quick charge ability)?. I think if just two batteries are being charged, then they go in the center, in the #1 and #2 spots-- so that's my plan going forward. I imagine this information is in the little pamphlet that came with the package. I'll be back if I find it and learn anything.

--The charging batteries at no point has gotten too warm my Energizer one gets pretty warm).

MY THOUGHTS:
--I LOVE that it has the TWO charging cords, with LONG cords. First, I like that it even has a cord, period. I have the Energiizer one that is just plugged into the wall. It seems like it would take up less space, but it doesn't. I find it harder to use as I need perfect clearance to plug that thing in. With this, I just need to find an outlet, then I can have it placed further away, making it easier to see and access. With the addition of the car charger, it just adds another option. Nice for camping (flashlights, radio, etc), or if you still use non cellphone cameras that eat batteries like crazy (this is what originally got me into rechargeable batteries almost 20 years ago, the digital cameras- ugh, I'm old). I sometimes bring a speaker with me for use with smartphone. It takes AA batteries. If I think to actually carry this unit around with me, I can charge my speaker batteries on the go if need be. But I think I will use this primarily in my home. I go through batteries with use of a couple of lighted mirrors. I have one that takes 4AAA and one that takes 4AA. The lights are bright, and I tend to go through batteries- so I make sure to have rechargeables on hand. As mentioned before, I like this unit because it is easier for me to find a place to put it to plug in AND have resting nearby. I had been in need of recharging a set of batteries and just hadn't gotten around to it because I don't care for the inconvenient (to me) charging unit of the other one. It works great, but I just found I prefer to have a cord. This has a cord.

PICTURES include another brand of (depleted) rechargeable AA battery (2000mah) with start time of being placed in charging unit. Product info says AA batteries between 1800mah and 2300mah will take 2-2.5 hours to charge. I put in the batteries at 11:42 am, and at 2:18 pm they were still charging. This would be just over 2.5 hours. I got up to take my dogs outside, and when I came back an hour later, the batteries were fully charged. So, I would plan on anywhere between 2.5-3.5 for a full charge on a depleted set of batteries (from another brand). Since I have yet to fully deplete the ACDelco batteries, I can't test those out until I do.

In summation.. I find nothing wrong with it, it works mostly intended.. If I figure anything else out as I continue to use these, I will be back to update.
text_fidelity_b: ACDelco 2-Hour Fast Battery Charger Includes AA Rechargeable Batteries and Car Adapter, 4 Count

text_fidelity_a:
FDY MP3 Player, MP3 Player with Bluetooth5.0, 32GB Portable Music Player with FM Radio/Recorder, HiFi Lossless Sound Quality, 2.4Inch Touch Screen Mini MP3 Player for Running, Expandable 128GB TF When I opened the package containing this MP3 player, I was amazed at how small it is. But immediately became delighted at its perfectly small size. It is not the size of a small cellphone, but rather like what should have naturally occurred if an iPod shuffle mated with an iPod Nano. Perfect size and perfect function.

As the product description does not list or show the size of this MP3 player I list them here:

Length: 2 3/4 inches Width: 2 inches Thickness: 3/8 inch

Yes, small, but a powerhouse in functionality. I really miss the days when an MP3 player just played music. After a near fatal fall of my phone (luckily just the screen protector cracked!) it became important that an expensive phone might not be the best thing to lug around while performing yardwork. This excellent device solves that issue, and solves it well.

Songs and MP3 audio books were loaded easily onto the player. It is not made by Apple nor is part of their line, so the iTunes program does not work with this. However, it is a easy fix - just go to your Music folder on your computer, and drop the files you wish into this device's memory. Easy peasy and quick. It comes with an included 32 GB of memory, but can easily be upgraded if you install your own micro SD card, up to 128 GB.

It comes with wired earphones, which I did not use or test. With the invention of easy to pair Bluetooth earphones, I have no desire to be ever tethered with a headphone cord again. The player pairs easily with all 3 of my Bluetooth devices - earphones, headphones, and speakers. The sound from each device is flawless, which might be a function of the device, but is also determined by the source.

There are just 3 buttons on the side of this MP3 player - on/off button, volume up, and volume down. All other functions are controlled by the small but well designed touch screen. It is very comparable with the touch capability of modern phones, the programs are opened with ease and operate in an intuitive logical manner. There are other functions built into this device, but since I really got it as an MP3 player, that is what I am focused upon.

With this player comes a handy removable back clip, letting you clip it on/in a pocket, armband, belt, anywhere. Without the clip, it is small enough to easily slip into any pocked of your cloths, even the tiny change pockets in most jeans. Besides the wired earphones & clip, there is a 3mm audio cable for attaching it manually to another device, and a Micro USB cable for charging. There is a plastic protective film on the front face - it can be removed, but the touch screen operates just fine if it is left on.

This is my new favorite toy, It it not cheap or flimsy, but in all honesty, looks and feels like a tiny cell phone in how its constructed. It does not happen often, but this wonderful MP3 player exceeded my expectations.
text_fidelity_b: FDY MP3 Player, MP3 Player with Bluetooth5.0, 32GB Portable Music Player with FM Radio/Recorder, HiFi Lossless Sound Quality, 2.4Inch Touch Screen Mini MP3 Player for Running, Expandable 128GB TF

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba Canvio Basics 1TB Portable Hard Drive - Black (HDTB310XK3AA) PERFECT!

I was looking for a MAC time machine backup drive and noticed the external drives labeled as MAC were $10 - $15 more. I then read the Q&A on this drive and someone gave the most perfect instructions:

"right out of the box it's not Mac ready, but the solution is real easy. You go to Utilities and open up Disk Utility. With the drive plugged in, select it and go to the Erase tab and there should be a drop down menu with Format. Select Mac OS and click erase and after that's done, the drive should be formatted for Mac and you can save to your heart's content."

I might only add where to find Disk Utility in case you didn't know ... in finder go to the applications folder and in that folder is utilities and in that folder is disk utility.

I did just as the person in Q&A said and the second it was done reformatting a box came up asking if I wanted to use this drive as a time machine backup drive. I said yes, and within 107 seconds I was done. Color me impressed!

We got the 1tb drive because we have a 1tb 21.5" iMac from Nov 2013.

I hope this helps someone. I will update this review later as to longevity of the drive.

UPDATE: May 6, 2018
7 months later and this little backup drive does what it should do. We have never needed to utilize the files it stores, but it is nice to know the files are there. I periodically check to make sure my Mac is recording on this drive and it functions perfectly as a time machine drive.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba Canvio Basics 1TB Portable Hard Drive - Black (HDTB310XK3AA)

TECKNET Wireless Mouse, 2.4G Ergonomic Optical Mouse, Computer Mouse for Laptop, PC, Computer, Chromebook, Notebook, 6 Buttons, 24 Months Battery Life, 2600 DPI, 5 Adjustment Levels I've used several mice before, and this is without a doubt the most uncomfortable mouse I've ever put my hands on. My hands are pretty small for a guy, and I was looking for something to replace my Logitech M705 that died. This mouse looks almost identical, if not better. However, I noticed immediately after putting batteries in it (none came with it) and plugging the dongle into the computer that there was a slight lag in comparison to the low quality wired Dell mouse I've been using temporarily. I can deal with a slight delay, especially since the movement didn't appear choppy, just delayed. The second thing I noticed was how poorly placed the forward/backward buttons are. You cannot avoid the buttons, and are forced to either rest you thumb on the buttons or on the desk, which I find uncomfortable. The "Ergonomic" design of the mouse was poorly designed and does not fit in your hand well at all--no matter what position I held the mouse, there was a constant pressure on my thumb, and I could never completely grip the mouse. I tried getting used to it, and used it for maybe an hour before becoming furious with how uncomfortable it is in my hands. I now have a mouse that will never be used and will likely donate it, since you cannot return it. I should have just gone with the Logitech. Yet another victim to high ratings and low cost.

tl;dr Do not get this mouse.
text_fidelity_b: TECKNET Wireless Mouse, 2.4G Ergonomic Optical Mouse, Computer Mouse for Laptop, PC, Computer, Chromebook, Notebook, 6 Buttons, 24 Months Battery Life, 2600 DPI, 5 Adjustment Levels

PANASONIC Bluetooth Wireless Headphones with Microphone and Call / Volume Controller - RP-HF400B-K - On-Ear Headphones (Black) I have worked with a lot of Bluetooth headphones, all of which have their strengths and weaknesses. These headphones by Panasonic are on the less expensive end. The question is whether they are worth the asking price. In my opinion, they could be better and are still priced a little high.

Comfort-wise, I do not care for these but this is a personal preference. I like a headphone that fits tightly and presses down on my head, and these are very light-fitting. They adjust well enough and there should not be too much trouble getting these to fit almost any head, but keep in mind that they’re not the type that clamps down tightly.

The build quality is sub-par. These are very lightweight and feel quite flimsy and fragile.

I found an issue in the sound profile. The bass is good and not too heavy, and that’s good news for me. I dislike strong bass which is good for giving me headaches. The midrange is on target too and the music has some depth. Where the problem lies is in the highs. When listening to music I noticed some distortion in the highs. It’s not in-your-face and it doesn’t ruin the listening experience unless you are really fussy about your music. These will be fine for listening to speech, though.

I had no trouble connecting these to my laptop via Bluetooth. These come up quickly and connect without any issue and are ready to go in seconds. These aren’t the absolute fastest connecting phones I have worked with but they are among the faster ones I have used.

There’s no protective case for these phones in the box, not even a sleeve. These do fold up nice and compactly but I am not sure what is the point without a case in which to store them.

As I write this, the asking price for these phones is $60 which is a bit high in my eyes. If the sound profile was perfect, or if the build quality was higher, I would be more amenable to that price but the truth is that less expensive phones can be found that have a better sound profile and are constructed more solidly - and they have a case.

These are not bad phones, but I think they leave much to be desired. The build quality is mediocre, the sound profile is imperfect and the cost is a little high for what is in the box.
text_fidelity_b: PANASONIC Bluetooth Wireless Headphones with Microphone and Call / Volume Controller - RP-HF400B-K - On-Ear Headphones (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 360 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Text-To-Speech (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I've had this Nuvi 360 since Dec, 2006. It really works well. I carried it with me to DC. Even on foot it was terrific. It knew where all the restaurants and points of interest were and faithfully navigated us around the ancient horse paths of the Virginia/DC area. Believe me, when you pop out of an underground Metro station in the middle of the night and have no idea where you are or which direction to head off in, the ol' Garmin was there.

It's so small it easily fits in a pocket. The built-in battery lasts reasonably long. In the car, the 12-Volt adapter allows the unit to stay on indefinitely. You can select which accent and which gender you want the voice prompts to speak. Australian "Bruce," American "Jill" and a host of other combinations. All very fun. The voice prompts are the best. You really don't need to look at the thing while driving because it's uncanny in telling you what to do when you need to do it. It is amazingly accurate: something like 20 feet. It takes you right to the destination driveway.

It acquires the sats quickly and doesn't get flustered if you violate its recommendation and go in a different route. It just says, "recalculating" and finds another route for you. None of this "make a U-turn, bonehead!" It gives you enough time to make the turns, too. Also, it displays how far it is until the next turn. Very nice. No need to worry if you've missed it.

If you are planning on going to Europe, buy the unit that comes preloaded with both US and Europe maps as purchasing the Europe maps after the fact will really jump the cost unnecessarily.

I haven't used the Bluetooth capability yet but might later...after I get a Bluetooth phone.

The display is quite viewable in daylight and very bright at night, though it can be set to auto-dim at sundown so it's not too bright at night. You can touch the screen and scroll the map under your finger much like Google Maps can, to preview your route if desired. It shows coordinates and you can save them as destinations if desired, even if the location doesn't have an official street address. It is an MP3 player and can display photos and play Audible books on tape. When you are using the MP3 or Audible features, it pauses the file playing back to announce directions, then returns to the file without losing any of the MP3 file or book info. Very nice.

At extra cost, it has the ability to add foreign language dictionaries which can verbally speak phrases and words to you. You can also add Travel Guides and other software via the SD chip slot.

Overall, I'm very pleased with this device. It's accurate, fast, functional and small.

The one thing that doesn't work is the windshield suction mount. It broke before I even used it once. The plastic loops on the suction cup that receive the ball arm's hinge pin are too thin and fragile and broke with just a little normal hinge adjustment.

I recommend the model 010-10908-00 friction mount that looks like a bean bag with a ball arm sticking up. I made something similar by taking an unneeded 1/4" thick mousepad and epoxying a couple of small 1" x 1" angle brackets to the pad to hold the ball arm that I salvaged from the broken suction cup mount.

A friction mount is interchangeable with multiple vehicles, doesn't slide around on the dash and allows complete and rapid removal and/or hiding to avoid theft. Plus, you don't have to glue a disk to the dash for the suction cup to attach to.

UPDATE 10-22-07:
The 360 works well enough; better than most. It should: Five point three bills should deliver one heck of a map!

I've had it since Dec 2006...less than one year. Today I get an offer from Garmin to update my North American map software for a mere point seven bills. That's AFTER the five point three bills I already sunk into this little electronic gizmo.

I heard Garmin has a one year free map update policy, but their website won't let me do it. Not cool. The cost of the unit has already fallen significantly from what I originally paid and now they want more to get it current, within a year of purchase. Not cool at all. Also, impossible to contact by email. Garmin website is in a permanent loop back to itself when clicking on the "contact by email" option. Otherwise, it's call and wait on hold between certain times. Not cool again.

Then a friend says how well his Verizon GPS works on his wireless phone. I look into that. Verizon offers a full time GPS cost and a single use option for under three bucks per use.

For what I have wasted on this Garmin--over five bills and counting upward forever with their unfriendly updates--that's a whole heck of a lot of one-time Verizon uses with what will be the most updated, most accurate database. After all, no one's going to beat the phone company with accurate phone numbers and addresses.

If I hadn't already bought into the Garmin ripoff, I'd definitely go with Verizon's phone based GPS: the phone will always be with you when you need it instead of in the glove compartment in the other car.

And it most likely won't get stolen. It's a darned pain to have to put the Garmin away after each use so some cretin won't bash in a window to steal a very, very expensive toy that could just as easily fit inside a phone.

Go with the phone.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 360 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Text-To-Speech (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Seagate Wireless Plus 1TB Portable Hard Drive with Built-in WiFi (STCK1000100) I intended to give the [[ASIN:B00AQRUW4Q Seagate Wireless Plus 1 TB Mobile Device Storage with Built-In Wi-Fi Streaming (STCK1000100)]] a rating of four stars, but have decided that it really is a five star product. The near deduction was because of the frustration I experienced in my attempting to get the device up and running with the limited information provided in the package and on the website. Once I successfully downloaded the software to my Droid, Kindle Fire and MacBook, I still encountered more trial and error than usual until I was able to figure out how the darn thing works. Fast forward to days and weeks of loving the device!

The Wireless Plus can be used as an extra drive for storage if you're not interested in using it for streaming, but if that's your true need, I'd likely recommend purchasing something else. With it's own Wi-Fi streaming, you don't need to use your home or hot network. Using it's Wi-Fi has been quick and has been glitch free for us thus far. We have used three devices at once and found it to be problem-free, with no freezes, crashes or difficulties. We had it up and running for four hours and still had battery power, then recharged. Although it can be charged via the USB on your computer, it is much faster by plugging it into an electrical outlet if one's available. Since we haven't drained the battery yet, I can't say how long it really lasts.

Music, movies, pictures, documents, audiobook, you can use whichever you want on any networked device as long as the device has the appropriate application installed. I watched the Seagate tutorials several times and found them to be difficult to follow, however once I spent some dedicated time just feeling my way through, I discovered that I do like the applications, too. Even if I'm not accessing the Wireless Plus on my Droid, I have been using the Seagate app.

This arrives with little documentation, but it is USB 3 capable if you need it. The housing is lightly rubberized and it has a matte metal plate in a charcoal gray color on the face side. The plug appears to be proprietary, the second reason I almost deducted a star from this review. It looks like a hybrid mini plug that's attached via a thin wire, not a cable, to a USB for either a device or the two prong electrical plug. No case is included, but I have a couple that work great. The size isn't so big that it feels cumbersome, but it is heavier than it appears to be upon first glance. I don't mind the weight because this little device holds 1 TB, much more than I have loaded on it as of today. I highly recommend this device and look forward to Seagate upgrading it as time passes. It's unique and not expensive for what it offers.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate Wireless Plus 1TB Portable Hard Drive with Built-in WiFi (STCK1000100)

text_fidelity_a:
Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation) The Flip is a pint-sized camcorder with a surprising feature set given its compactness. Though is it not a full-featured camcorder and I would not recommend it for serious recording (special events or production material), it is excellent for on-the-go shots and for spontaneous recording when opportunities present themselves.

The Flip is small - a little smaller than an ice cream sandwich. It may be little, but there's tremendous convenience in being able to drop your camcorder in your shirt pocket or your purse and have it at the ready. This compact size holds everything you need to start recording - batteries, flash RAM and all. Without tapes or DVD media on which to record, there's little reason for this device to be any bigger.

It is a solid little thing and feels durable. That doesn't mean it would do well if dropped or stepped on, but it likely will be ok if jostled a little.

Recording is simple. No, I should be more clear - recording with the Flip is trivial. There is no real science to using it: turn it on, point and press record. Press the record button again to stop recording. Even technological novices, or people afraid of electronics will have no trouble using the Flip to record. Playing back is equally simple - once the recording is finished, press the Play button.

There are + and - buttons, used for Zoom. The Flip doesn't have a particularly capable zoom, so shooting from a distance will not yield especially great results.

I tested this camcorder in my basement on a bright, sunny day, and I wandered about recording and chattering to myself. When I played back what I had recorded, I made a pleasant discovery - it does some light balancing and deals with changes in light levels so that the video is still clear. The sound is also good, better than I expected. When I walked down a dark hallway and into an unlit room, it had tried very hard to accommodate for the lack of light but it was unable to completely overcome the darkness. As there is no light on the camcorder to come on when it is dark, this is understandable, but it did surprisingly well in spite of that.

I attached the Flip to my computer to pull the video to my hard drive. FlipShare installed itself and started up, seeing the video I had made. It allowed me to pull it over and even gave me the option to delete it from the camera. Once finished, I was able to play the video through FlipShare. Instead, I decided to hunt it down and use a different application to play it.

I found the file and tried to open it with Windows Media Player. I got audio, but not video. When I switched to QuickTime, my video came up and filled my screen. This is the point at which I made an unfortunate discovery. Every minute move I had made while recording was now plainly obvious, as there is no anti-jitter built into the device.

The video, on a 1440x900 resolution screen, looked clear. It records at 1280x720, which is not that much smaller, so I was a little surprised. I would have expected a little pixelation, but this actually was not an issue.

There are few settings that can be adjusted on the Flip - language, date, time and recording light.

The Flip is a nice camcorder that provides tremendous convenience and fun. It is very easy to use and very compact. It is important to remember that it has some limitations which make it a less-than-ideal choice for more serious application, but if those limitations are not an issue for you then the Flip is a fun and affordable way to capture things on video.
text_fidelity_b: Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation)

GreatShield (3 Pack) Ultra Anti-Glare (Matte) Clear Screen Protector Film for Amazon Kindle Fire (Does Not Fit Kindle Fire HD) I keep being offered this product to review through the "Your Review Helped" emails I get, even though I've already reviewed it through Vine, so I'll take this opportunity to offer an update. The screen smudges easily with the Great Shield protector applied, and it's hard to clean it. I've subsequently had an opportunity to review the Moshi product, and it is hands-down the best of the two. The clarity of the Moshi screen is better than the Great Shield, and it's easier to apply. I've accordingly bumped the Great Shield down to three stars now that I have something better for comparison.

Original review through Amazon Vine:

Okay, like some other reviewers, I had a frustrating experience getting this anti-glare screen protector installed properly on my Kindle Fire. When you buy this three-pack, figure they are giving you two hands-on lessons in how to install it! (Considering I paid over twice as much for just one Zagg screen protector for my Kindle 2, the price for this Fosmon product is still very reasonable.) I had read all the reviews and warnings before I began, and I still ruined my first two.

First, who lives in a "dust-free environment"? You have to be very careful. You should first shake any dust off the protector itself; after I'd failed to install the first two, I used one of the wipes that came with them to wipe down both sides of my last protector to clear it of all packing dust that it arrived with. Then clean your Fire screen, including the cracks around the sides of the screen. Clean it again. And again.

My first effort went very well until I went to remove the #2 (face) plastic. I didn't realize I had to very slowly pull up on the tab to get the top piece started coming away from the actual shield protector before pulling—so I pulled the whole thing off! One down, two to go. On my second effort, I didn't quite get the protector perfectly positioned so I had a very slight overlap on the right-hand side, resulting in a large unattached area. Unusable. The third time, I folded the #1 plastic down halfway, just so I could hold the protector flat above my Fire and not touch the actual protector (to avoid fingerprints), edged the upper right corner in perfectly straight, anchored it across the top, and then let the protector kind of glide itself onto the screen as I pulled off the remaining #1 plastic. I had some larger bubbled areas, but I did not try to use the little cardboard piece to squeegee them out; I used my thumbs to press outward toward the nearest edge. This gave me a near-perfect installation. I carefully removed the #2 plastic, slipped my Fire back into its [[ASIN:B005QBK5V2 rooCASE Dual-View Multi Angle (Black) 100% Genuine Leather Leather Folio Case Cover for Amazon Kindle Fire 7-Inch Android Tablet]], tucked one of the little squares of screen-cleaning cloth behind the Fire for later cleaning use if needed, and it was all good to go.

After regularly fighting the glare from my Kindle Fire, it took me a little while for my eyes to adjust to the difference with the anti-glare shield protector in place, but I LIKE it! Reading is now easier on my eyes, and my [[ASIN:B005EM6IAA GreatShield 2-in-1 Ballpoint Pen and Capacitive Touchscreen Stylus for Amazon Kindle Fire Tablet]] seems to be working with more precision than it was before. Despite the hassles, I do recommend this product and I'm glad I've got it.
text_fidelity_b: GreatShield (3 Pack) Ultra Anti-Glare (Matte) Clear Screen Protector Film for Amazon Kindle Fire (Does Not Fit Kindle Fire HD)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging I have a Nuvi 360. It came with a suction cup windshield mount. It also came with a steel disk with double sticky adhesive on the back. I was supposed to mount this disk somewhere on my dashboard, then use the suction cup to attach the mount. I didn't want to use the suction mount directly onto the windshield because 1) it telegraphs the presence of an expensive GPS unit, 2) it's illegal in California to attach anything to the windshield and 3) I don't think the suction cup would last very long.

Then there's the disk with the very permanent double sticky tape. The problem with almost all cars these days is there really isn't anywhere to attach the disk discreetly. Every square inch is taken with existing stuff. And who wants an ugly disk glued to the dash anyway? And what if I want to use the GPS in other vehicles? More disks?

So I settled on this "beanbag" mount with the ball mount arm.

Unfortunately, before the beanbag friction mount arrived, I was flexing the arm in the suction cup mount and noticed the suction cup's mounting bracket had already broken. I had never even attached it to anything! The mount is beautifully engineered and built...except for one area where the arm's hinge pin attaches to the suction cup's plastic hinge loops. The loops are too thin and fragile. The loops cracked and broke with hardly any hinging at all.

So now I have a quite useless suction mount but a very functional ball arm. What to do?

I drove the hinge pin out of the ball arm. Then I took two small 1" x 1" steel angle brackets and attached them to the ball arm with a 2" long, 8-32 threaded machine screw and an 8-32 wingnut. This created two "feet" for the ball arm. Then I epoxied the two bracket "feet" to the fabric (upper) side of an old 1/4" thick mousepad. Ta da. A friction pad for pennies with a ball arm attached.

Works great. Cost was virtually nothing. Doesn't slide on either of the two dashboards I've tried it on. The mousepad is flexible and conforms easily to the curving shape of the various dashboards. It doesn't weigh much but the thick mousepad has enough heft to plant the getup nicely. The grippy rubber side of the mousepad adheres nicely to the dash. Yet I can pull it down to the floor quickly and reposition it easily.

I wish I'd thought of this BEFORE I ordered this "official" friction mount to the tune of a couple of twenties.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging

text_fidelity_a:
VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones.

The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup.

I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.
text_fidelity_b: VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube

LG Electronics 49UJ6300 49-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2017 Model) This television has absolutely vibrant colors and a noticeably smooth, fast refresh rate (120 hz). It has good preset picture modes depending on what sort of programming or ambience you need. The sports mode works wonderfully for ice hockey!

There is an Energy Savings setting (under Settings>All Settings (3 dots at bottom of list) which significantly dims the screen and makes darks too dark. Turning this mode to OFF will make your screen vibrant as you likely expect it to be.

The built in speakers aren't terrific, and the only sound output is optical. There are only 3 HDMI outputs so if you use multiple devices be prepared to swap them out.

The TV comes with its own preset apps which covers many of the popular ones, though LG still doesn't carry the HBO Now app.

Despite those shortcomings, I would purchase this TV again. We paid $699 with Prime shipping whereas our local big box stores carried the same model for $150 more. The freight company brought the TV up to the door so we didn't have to worry about how to get it home even if a local store was able to price match.

text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras I've always wanted a Canon macro flash but the cost was just too much for something that I would not use very regularly. This macro light, while not a flash, is a very affordable alternative that works very well.

It is a 48 LED light. There's no communication with the camera - it's not a flash, nor can it be controlled in any way by the camera itself. The controls are manual, and allow you to use all the LEDs, half of them (left) or half of them (right). It is powered by 2 AA batteries or by an AC adapter (included). The battery pack mounts on the hotshoe, and the macro light is affixed to the lens barrel.

The battery pack fit fine on my Canon 5D Mark II, but the manufacturer includes a note with the device that says an additional adapter will be needed for it to fit the hotshoe of Sony, Konica and Minolta DSLR cameras.

It comes with two diffusers (white and orange) that are easy to put on and take off. It also comes with six lens thread adapter rings for all the usual sizes - 49mm, 52, 55, 58, 62, and 67. You attach the adapter ring to front of lens, and slot the light over the ring.

No problems fitting it to a Canon L 100mm macro lens. Fit well and was secure during use.

It throws a good amount of light on a ultra close-range subject, which may be otherwise shaded by the close proximity of your lens, or for other reasons be hard to light properly. But, there are limitations - don't expect this to throw a lot of light like a light panel would on a subject at medium distance.

The build quality is better than expected given the price. It's all plastic, but seems more than durable enough for home use.

I'm very pleased with this. It's a small fraction of the cost of a Canon ring light and, while it does not have flash capabilities, it remains a very helpful addition to lighting those tricky macro shots. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras

Once I installed the card and rebooted, the NVMe didn't show in the files list, but it hadn't been formatted. It showed right up in the Gnome disks utility. I benchmarked it immediately, and, wow. Those speeds may not look like much to those who have later gen equipment, but the speeds were impressive for this older system.

It looks like I could have made it my primary drive, but I think I would choose to use this SSD as a personal cloud storage device in a USB enclosure. But enclosures for this particular 2280 (22mm X 80mm) form factor and NVMe are still rather pricey. I'm guessing the prices will come down eventually. Until then, the more economical option is to get an inexpensive adapter card and install it in a desktop PC, or install it in a laptop that has an M.2 slot and will accommodate 80mm long cards.

It looks like a good way to get some fast speeds and big capacity into some older gear. I'll leave the more technical reviews for the more technically minded.
text_fidelity_b: Crucial P1 1TB 3D NAND NVMe PCIe Internal SSD, up to 2000MB/s - CT1000P1SSD8

text_fidelity_a:
ClearClick HD Video Capture Box Ultimate (4K Edition) - Record and Stream Video from HDMI (Up to 4K30) and AV Video Sources - No Computer Required THE GOOD:
--------------
* It will do as it says.. capture videos from your sources.
* Video quality seems fine to me. I'm not that picky, the stuff I record isn't important.
* You can install a micro SD card, or connect a hard drive via usb.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Consistent with their products, they cut corners when it comes to the remote control. It's just a terrible clunky experience. I can't even put into words what's wrong with it. I guess there is a delay. So if you're impatient, you'll be pressing too many buttons, and you'll be in the wrong menu, navigate to the wrong places, enable the wrong features, etc. So my advice is to be patient. Press the button you want to press, then wait a week for it to respond. I don't know what inner components make a great remote control. Whatever they are, they are not inside ClearClick remotes. I've reviewed some of their other Clearclick products that are $150 and less, and so I was more forgiving. But at $250, really? You're going to still skimp out on the remote at this price range?

* If you toggle into PLAYBACK mode... good luck getting out of it. Back button doesn't work, and it's always thinking you want to delete files. Everytime I escape playback mode, I'm relieved, but also have no clue how I got out.

* Power on/off is weird. There are scenarios that will make your heart stop because you'll think the device shorted out. Just like their terrible remotes, I've noticed this power issue with their other models too. The quirk is this... sometimes when you power off and on too quickly, it just goes dead. It will not respond for a long time. Don't panic. Stop pushing the power button. Just unplug everything. The hard drive, the HDMI, the power, unplug everything. Go walk your dog, and when you come back, and connect everything again, it will power up. This happens to other Clearclick devices I have, so when it happened with this device, I didn't panic. I knew what was up.

* Power port is micro usb. Again, at $250, I'd like to see USB-C. Micro usb is antiquated, and their cords are prone to get damaged.

* You will need a HDMI splitter to bypass HDCP, as well as be able to turn off your Clearclick when you're not recording, and still watch TV. In my scenario... my source goes into my splitter, and my splitter has TWO outs. One goes into the Clearclick, and the other goes to my projector. This way, I can turn off my Clearclick if I'm not recording, and still watch my projector. If I connect the source directly to the Clearclick, and then go OUT from the Clearclick to my projector, then I would get their ugly icons on my projector. In my pictures, the source is my Nvidia Shield, you'll notice a row of white icons at the top. There is no option to hide these icons in passthrough mode. So if you use the Clearclick as a passthrough, you will get those ugly icons on your big screen. So even if you're recording sources that do not need a HDMI splitter. I'd still get one anyway because using the hdmi passthrough is not pretty. However, the good thing is that the files you record, will not have those icons.

In conclusion, if this weren't a Vine item, I would send it back. Having said all that, it's possible that my expectations may be unreasonable for a very niche product. If a big company like Sony or Samsung create a polished standalone capture device like this, maybe it'd be $500-$600. In which case, you'd be pretty happy with the ClearClick. If you learn to live with the quirks, it's a nifty piece of tech. Hopefully, they can improve on the user experience through firmware updates. I'll go 3-Stars this time.
text_fidelity_b: ClearClick HD Video Capture Box Ultimate (4K Edition) - Record and Stream Video from HDMI (Up to 4K30) and AV Video Sources - No Computer Required

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire HD 8.9", 8.9" HD display, 16 GB or 32 GB, Wi-Fi or Optional 4G LTE Wireless (Previous Generation - 2nd) As with the original Fire, the out of box experience is very nicely done. Very straightforward process of just turning it on and letting the tablet register and update itself. It took about 10 minutes (with the majority of the time waiting for an update to download) and it was ready to go. It picked up all my original Fire music and books from the cloud and most of my Fire apps. I was disappointed to see that a couple of my favorite apps (TED Talks and Play Music Videos Free) were judged not compatible with my new Fire. Hopefully updates will be coming soon.

The screen is delightful! Crisp and clear, and a marked increase in resolution versus the original Fire. Videos on the HD Fire are simply amazing.

The sound quality is also a marked improvement. While it was pretty much mandatory to hook up an external speaker for the original Fire, the new Fire puts out pretty decent sound quality all on its own. I still hook it up to external speakers (I'm partial to the Bose Companion 20) for movies and music when I'm at my desk, but it puts out more than adequate sound all on its own.

Response time is more snappy than the original Fire, and the carousel is easier to navigate (smoother scrolling). Picking up a WiFi signal seems to be better with the new fire - I'm getting all signal strength bars displayed in areas of the house where I could only get 2 or 3 bars with the original Fire.

The form factor is great for video watching. The extra screen size makes a big difference. The other huge advantage to the size is typing. It's MUCH easier to see and use the onscreen keyboard than on the original Fire. I had no problems typing without a stylus; on the original Fire a stylus is a must.

So far I don't see many misses other than a hard-to-find power button. The casing and build quality is not at the same level as an iPad, but neither is the price. I'm very pleased with the price-performance level of the HD Fire.

This is not replacing my original Fire - I'll continue to use that for most of my book reading and when I need portability. For everything else, the larger screen is well worth the additional cost.

I have a Nexus 7, the iPad 2 and an HP Touchpad and the Fire is my favorite by far. Not because either the original or this new Fire are the best in terms of build quality or speed or tech specs, but for one simple reason: the Fire makes it so incredibly easy to avail myself of entertainment and content. The tight link to the Amazon ecosystem is, for me, a huge plus - it keeps my entertainment pipeline full of things I want to read, listen to or watch with little or no effort on my part. And, best of all, a lot of that content is free through Prime.

Love it, and highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire HD 8.9", 8.9" HD display, 16 GB or 32 GB, Wi-Fi or Optional 4G LTE Wireless (Previous Generation - 2nd)

text_fidelity_a:
ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).
If you want to spring for the subscription service, there's a TON of goodies and advanced features beyond even the cloud storage things. But even without that, the live view and photo motion alerts combined with the voice assistant / Alexa integration makes it worth it even just for the hardware alone!
text_fidelity_b: ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers This is by far the best ereader on the market.

The bad.

It doesn't do epub and it doesn't connect to the library. This seems like a deal breaker until you try to borrow a book from the library. I have one on hold now (to read on either the nook or the Sony) that should be available in 39 weeks. I'll probably give up and just buy it anyway.

The good.

The speed. The page turns are as fast as the average person can turn a print page. You won't see that "opening book" message the nook displays. When you tell it to open a book, it opens in less than a second. I keep hitting the page turn key just to marvel at how fast it is. I've never seen an ereader this fast. This is perfect.

Store access. Let me run you through buying a book for the various devices. For the Kindle, if you're on the Amazon site you select your book, click buy now, pick up the device and start reading. For the nook, you buy the book, then you turn on the touch screen that keeps turning itself off, you go into the home screen, go to "My Library", select "Update B&N Content" and wait a few minutes. There is no mechanism to automatically push content to the device. For the Sony (I'm using the Daily Edition, which has 3G), you use the custom software (no way to buy from a website), buy the book, then either transfer it via USB, or go to the device, to the store, log into your account (you need to provide your login information each time you go to the store) find the book you bought and click download, then wait. For buying from the device, Kindle is easy and fast, nook is decent, and Sony is unreasonably slow.

The screen. There is no glare, even with the book light on. It's the crispest and easiest to read screen out there. It's beautiful.

Audible integration. Download your books via WiFi or transfer via USB and listen with your device, either through headphones or the speakers. How cool is that? Now if only there were a card reader to store those larger files.

Collections. I have the Kindle 1, so I was first introduced to collections via Sony. It's great to be able to organize so much content. Here you can organize ebooks and audiobooks into collections together. That's one thing Kindle and Sony both have over nook--they treat content the same. Nook is the only one that doesn't let you annotate or bookmark newspapers and magazines, and who wouldn't want to mark an article to refer back to later?

Ease of use. I handed my Kindle 1 to a woman who was too scared of technology to turn on her own laptop. Her husband had to do it for her. I wanted to show her a passage in the Declaration of Independence, and I had the passage on the screen. I didn't instruct her. Moments later, she turned the page and just kept reading, all the way the end. Then she looked at what else I had on the device. An ereader should be as easy and intuitive to use as a print book, and most of us figured those out when we were about 10 months old. Kindle fits that bill.

Social networking. Post passages and comments on them to Twitter and Facebook. You can see what passages other readers have highlighted. This is particularly great for online book clubs.

More language sets. I'm kind of hoping Amazon will sell Japanese language books in the US Kindle store, or let us buy from Amazon.co.jp.

I could go on and on, but what it comes down to is, when it comes down to the core features of an ereader--buying, reading, annotating, and searching a book, Kindle beats the competition hands down. When it comes to extra bells and whistles--organization, commenting to others, web access, text to speech, Kindle beats the competition hands down.

There is no other viable choice any more. Kindle is just too much better than every other device out there.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers

I honestly was not expecting to be as nice as it is.

I can speak from experience when I say that cats, coffee, and a MacBook are NOT a great combination. I lost an earlier MacBook Pro when cat and coffee collided over the keyboard, so when I purchased my new MacBook Air 13", I knew I wanted a keyboard cover.

This one has a lot going for it. It fits beautifully -- lays flat, the key covers are precisely where they should be, there's no slippage or any feeling of insecurity about the cover shifting position. It's transparent except for the colored key caps, so the underlighting of the MacBook Air keyboard shines through. It's quite thin so it doesn't add much in the way of bulk, either -- but the material feels like it will survive heavy use without tearing or puncturing.

I especially like having all the keyboard shortcuts printed right on the keys themselves. My version, the OX X shortcuts, is easy to read, and the colors actually mean somthing (blue = primary shortcuts, pink = finder, green = safari, orange = iWorks/Mail/MS Office). It's a nice touch that lends a bit of color to the rather drab aluminum face of the MacBook.

If you've never typed on a keyboard with a cover, it might take a little getting used to. It has a "softer" feel, but key action/etc. is not compromised at all.

Overall, I think this is a good product, a nice gift for someone with a new MacBook, with bult-in usefulness beyond protecting the keyboard from inadvertent spills and dust.

(Although a sample was supplied for review purposes, opinions expressed are based on my personal experience with this product.)

I shoot a lot of 4k video on Sony cameras, so I very much appreciate being able to copy lots of high bitrate footage after a shoot VERY quickly, which is exactly what this does!
You can always spot the UHS-II cards by their extra pins on the back. With a reader that can utilize them, I found this card performed pretty excellent in my benchmarks! 257MB/s read and a whopping 248MB/s write! That's incredible speed for write, I wasn't expecting it. On my other cards, UHS-II boosted the read times to similar proportions but write was similar to regular U3 class SDXC cards. That this Ritz card can produce similar write times as the boosted read is pretty incredible! This might be my new favorite media.
text_fidelity_b: Ritz Gear 64GB High-Speed SDXC UHS-II SD Card, C10, U3, V90, Full-HD & 8K Memory Card for DSLR, Cinema-Quality Video Cameras

This is NOT the speaker that you simply grab and throw in the bag and go. This speaker is rather large and surprisingly VERY heavy.

The sound quality is nice but the bass is only ok in my opinion. I have another speaker which is made by Amazon that cost about $50 that has the exact same sound quality. It is loud but as with this bass, ive heard others that are louder and cost much less.

As I mentioned before, this sucker is HEAVY so while it may be water proof, if you were to drop in the river at any point it would go straight to the bottom never to be seen again, so it wouldn't really matter how water proof it is. One use that I can see us using this speaker would be for travel baseball games. It is loud enough that you would be able to hear it from a distance.

As I said earlier... some will love this speaker and think that it is absolutely worth it. Others will not. This speaker will strictly come down to personal opinion. For instance, other than the weight, I love this speaker. My spouse thinks that his $50 is much better.

Air Duster & Vacuum 2-in-1, Cordless Electric Compressed Air Blower for Computer Keyboard Cleaning Replaces Canned Air Spray, Portable Handheld Electronics Car Computer Duster, Powerful 77000RPM Motor I do a lot of work on sewing machines and electronics that need to be sprayed with air often. I was having a hard time with canned air working right or stopping working before it was gone. Then I saw this. I am never going back!

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a combo vacuum/blower. It has a clear blue top on it for catching dust and dirt, and then it is removable so that you can blow air on things with a simple switch on the side. There is a small hose extension for focused air flow.

CORD
This charges with a USB /micro USB cord.

VACUUM BRUSHES
This comes with two brushes. One fits on the extension bar and the other fits in the top of the clear blue catcher container.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
VACUUM
Honestly it is okay as a vacuum, but I have other vacuums that are cordless that I prefer. The only thing that this excels at for me is keyboard and other very fine cleaning. I don't find the suction as great as I would like and the blowing air from the vents is so heavy it blows things around as I move with the vacuum.

AIR BLOWING
For blowing, that is another story. This little gem is fabulous. I take the blue top off and put the switch at the blowing and it empties out my sewing machine bobbin area beautifully. It also blows out keyboard and other areas of the laptop that need cleaning.

CHARGES
I have used this since I got it for several weeks and it has not needed to be charged again. I only use it as needed, so it is probably going to stay charged for a while. It only took a little over and hour to charge when I got it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Nice to have as a little vacuum, this excels at blowing air. It is rechargeable so no need to buy any more cans of air that don't work or end up breaking. This is something I have wanted for a long time. I am thrilled to have it.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is fantastic. I absolutely love it. My husband is going to get one for his business too. He ain't touchin' mine! (grins)
text_fidelity_b: Air Duster & Vacuum 2-in-1, Cordless Electric Compressed Air Blower for Computer Keyboard Cleaning Replaces Canned Air Spray, Portable Handheld Electronics Car Computer Duster, Powerful 77000RPM Motor

However, it's too lightweight for my tastes. The “click” feels cheap to me and the scroll wheel is stiff. I won't send this Microsoft mouse back, but I wouldn't buy it again. I haven't had any problems with this mouse, it's just personal preference. I'll just use the Microsoft as a travel mouse. hulu plus,

Flixster
CinemaNow
Rhapsody
Picasa
AccuWEather
Twitter
Pandora
Target
Internet TV--horrible interface

To be honest, I wouldn't use most of these, so I'm not all that impressed with the Apps, though certainly they have the most needed on one in Netflix. screen is a bit too bright. Personally, I'd find it annoying, but others may not notice.

It's not a bad player at all, does most of what it needs to OK, but I definitely prefer our Sony for its larger app features and dimmer screen (it also feels more sturdy).

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red Samsung X5 External SSD Thunderbolt 3 (500 GB)
This drive is marketed as the fastest External SSD currently on the market. From my testing they are not overstating that claim. I was able to transfer 250Gig of data (using a 2016 MacBook Pro) to the Samsung X5 drive in just over 7 minutes.

The drive uses a magnesium alloy (rather than aluminum) for this case. This means that the drive will not throw off as much heat. Due to this fact the drive has thermal management which will slow the drive down (after extended use) to keep it from over heating. Just be aware of this should you need to move very large files back and forth.

Pros
- Very fast transfer rates
- Comes with Thunderbolt 3 cable
- Solid build quality

Cons
- Expensive. The T5 version is only $109.00 [hence the one star drop. If a tad less expensive, we would have given it the full five stars.]
- Drive may slow down when continually transferring large files due to thermal management.
- Only works with Thunderbolt 3 ports.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red

text_fidelity_a:
Aurum Cables Pack of 2 AUX 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Stereo Audio Cable - for iPhone, iPad or Smartphones - 12 Feet I received this pack as a review sample and quickly came to the conclusion that these are excellent for noise-free applications. The most critical test was when I used this cable to connect a pair of [[ASIN:B006MA9XXM Brainwavz HM5 Studio Monitor Headphones]] to my stereo. The sound was as neutral and noise free as when I used the high grade cable that came with the phones, so the claim of double shielding hold weight. I would not hesitate to recommend these to audiophiles or sound engineers.

In addition to the listening test I thoroughly inspected the physical characteristics. That revealed attention to detail like what appears to be copper cladding or gold plating on the tip, ring and sleeve portions of the connector. The barrel housing is also well constructed and is probably stainless steel. The strain reliefs on the ends are also well done and should protect the ends from internal breakdown even if you frequently handle the cable. The cable itself will stretch to a full twelve feet, but at rest is a little over a foot and a half.

What I did not test is the claim that this will fit most phones through their case. That's because the cases that I have on hand will accommodate regular cables. There is a chamfer on the barrel that houses the connector and it looks as though it will fit some of the more finicky iPhone 5 cases, but I cannot guarantee that it will for all cases.

These are top quality cables that should last a long time if properly handled and stored. If I do experience a premature failure I'll update this review to reflect that.
text_fidelity_b: Aurum Cables Pack of 2 AUX 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Stereo Audio Cable - for iPhone, iPad or Smartphones - 12 Feet

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft EKZ-00001 Modern Keyboard with Fingerprint ID I use laptops at home instead of tower systems, but I still prefer a stand-alone keyboard for most things. I have had very good success with Microsoft peripherals in the past so I had high expectations for this keyboard. So far, it works well enough but I have encountered a couple of snags that make it less than perfect.

This is a slim and efficiently designed keyboard and it is slightly wider than my 15.6” laptop. It’s the right size for me and I am happy with the dimensions when it comes to fitting it in my work space. No complaints there.

Set-up is a little on the tricky side. I tried to set it up for Bluetooth use without following the instructions first and got nowhere. It does not appear in the list of available devices so it could not be paired right off the bat, though my system does handle the Bluetooth standard. The instructions say to connect it via USB first, then turn it on and follow the set-up when Windows detects it. However, the instructions do not say that you must use the cable that came with the keyboard; I used a different one and failed, though the keyboard did work as a USB keyboard with that 3rd-party cable connected.

I’ll answer the very obvious question right now – I was able to get it working under Linux as a USB keyboard, but not as a Bluetooth keyboard. I am not sure if the problem is with the Bluetooth receiver in the system I tested or if the keyboard is just not compatible at all. I have an iPhone as well and it did not see the keyboard in the list of available devices. This is not a failure or a shortcoming of the keyboard – it operates very much in accordance with how it has been marketed, so getting it to work under Linux with Bluetooth would have been just a bonus. Interestingly, it says it can be set up to work under the Windows Phone platform which has been discontinued...

When I set it up under Windows 10, it did not go as the documentation said it would go. I did get the toast notification and I clicked as directed. It set everything up and said it was ready to go. It never allowed me to set up the fingerprint configuration and I have been unable to find any setting within Windows to allow me to revisit. So, I have a fingerprint reader that I can’t configure. Considering that this is being used in a home with a private computer with password protection this really isn’t a show-stopper but it would have been nice to mess with this technology.

In operation the keyboard is very responsive and so far I have been pleased with it except for one thing that I cannot seem to reconfigure. I prefer to have the function keys operate as function keys by default, instead of media keys. Without being able to find a keyboard configuration setting in the OS anywhere I have no way to reverse the default operation, which is to require pressing the Function key prior to hitting F1 – F12 to get them to default as function keys instead of media keys.

I do like this keyboard and it works well for my needs. The set-up isn’t bullet-proof though, and there are some behaviors it would be nice to change or reconfigure.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft EKZ-00001 Modern Keyboard with Fingerprint ID

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics Double Braided Nylon USB-C to USB-C 3.1 Gen 2 (10Gbps) Fast Charging Cable, 3A - 1-Foot, Dark Gray These are pricey USB cables, but you get what you pay for. If you just need a cable for charging your USB device, there are cheaper USB2.0 cables that will work just as well. Where these cables shine is data transfer. USB3.1 is tremendously faster than USB2.0 and these cables live up to the specification (as long as your devices support USB3.1). If your devices are USB2.0, these cables will still fit, but you have to live with USB2.0 speeds. This cable is also very well made with durable heavy duty connectors as well as a thick durable cable casing. I would not be surprised if this cable gives me years of use.
